title: Risk and Reward
concept: Investments with greater potential returns often involve greater uncertainty and a wider range of possible gains and losses.
learningObjective: Understand that potential return and uncertainty are related.
primaryMisconception: Higher risk always produces higher profit.
secondaryMisconceptions: A stable investment option can never lose purchasing power.
A high-return opportunity must be a better investment.
Risk only means how much profit an investment may produce.
keyTakeaway: Higher risk may create greater potential returns, but never guarantees them.

screens.title: Two Roads, One Destination
screens.content: One road looks steady. Another may be faster but has sharp turns. Which one reaches the destination first?
screens.illustration: Two roads lead towards the same financial goal. One is smooth and slower; the other is steep with shortcuts and warning signs.

screens.title: Your £1,000 Decision
screens.content: You have a fictional £1,000 to set aside for one year. Three options offer different levels of uncertainty.
screens.illustration: A £1,000 card sits above three unopened investment paths labelled Stable, Moderate, and High Risk.

screens.title: Three Different Paths
screens.content: The stable option may change little. The moderate option may move more. The high-risk option could rise sharply—or lose much more.
screens.illustration: Three value lines show narrow, medium, and wide possible movement ranges without displaying guaranteed outcomes.

screens.title: Potential Is Not a Promise
screens.content: A larger possible reward comes with more uncertainty. You must predict the range of outcomes, not search for a guaranteed winner.
screens.illustration: A reward arrow rises alongside a widening band of possible gains and losses.

screens.title: Which Result Is Guaranteed?
screens.question: Which statement about the three options is most accurate?

options.text: The highest-risk option will earn the most
options.response: Higher risk may create a larger possible gain, but it can also produce a larger loss.

options.text: The stable option cannot lose value
options.response: Its price may change less, but fees, inflation, or other risks can still reduce its real value.

options.text: More potential reward usually comes with more uncertainty
options.response: Correct. A wider range of possible results includes both larger gains and larger losses.

options.text: All three options should produce the same result
options.response: Different levels of uncertainty can create very different outcomes.

screens.title: Choose the Most Likely Range
screens.instruction: Review each fictional option. Predict the range of possible outcomes, then compare what could happen during favourable and difficult conditions.

educationalAssumptions: This is a fictional classroom comparison.
The time period is one year.
No real company, fund, savings product, or return rate is represented.
The outcome descriptions demonstrate uncertainty rather than predict actual performance.
Fees, taxes, inflation, and currency changes are simplified or excluded unless stated.
Lower price movement does not mean an option is completely risk-free.
Greater uncertainty may create greater potential returns and greater potential losses.
No option is presented as universally suitable or recommended.
Past results and professional management cannot guarantee future outcomes.

options.label: Stable Path
options.description: A fictional low-volatility option designed to change relatively little over one year.
characteristics: Lower potential for a large gain
Lower likelihood of a large price fall
Inflation may still reduce purchasing power

predictionQuestion.text: Which outcome range best fits the Stable Path?

predictionOptions.text: Small gain, little change, or small loss
Exactly the same return every year

predictionQuestion.educationalOutcome: Small gain, little change, or small loss
predictionQuestion.explanation: A stable option generally has a narrower range of possible results. It may reduce some uncertainty but cannot remove every risk.

options.label: Moderate Path
options.description: A fictional mixed investment containing both steadier and more changeable holdings.
characteristics: More growth potential than the stable option

predictionQuestion.text: Which outcome range best fits the Moderate Path?

predictionOptions.text: Complete loss is the only outcome

predictionQuestion.explanation: This option accepts more uncertainty for greater potential growth, but its result may still be positive, negative, or close to unchanged.

options.label: High-Risk Path
options.description: A fictional investment in an early-stage company with an uncertain future.
characteristics: The business may fail even if the idea appears promising

predictionQuestion.text: Which outcome range best fits the High-Risk Path?

predictionOptions.text: Only a small change is possible
Large gain, large loss, or another uncertain result

predictionQuestion.educationalOutcome: Large gain, large loss, or another uncertain result
predictionQuestion.explanation: High risk increases the range of possible outcomes. It may create greater upside, but it also increases the chance and size of potential losses.

scenarios.title: Favourable Conditions
scenarios.scenario: Business conditions are strong, customers are spending, and investor confidence rises.

possibleOutcomes.outcome: May produce a small positive result
May produce a moderate positive result
May produce a large gain, but this is not guaranteed

question.text: Which option has the greatest potential gain in this scenario?

predictionOptions.text: All outcomes are guaranteed to be equal

question.explanation: The high-risk option has the greatest upside potential, but potential does not mean the gain will occur.

scenarios.title: Difficult Conditions
scenarios.scenario: Demand falls, businesses struggle, and investors become more cautious.

possibleOutcomes.outcome: May experience a small decline or little change

question.text: Which option has the greatest potential loss in this scenario?

predictionOptions.text: None of the options can lose value

question.explanation: The wider possible outcome range works in both directions. Greater upside potential generally comes with greater downside risk.

scenarios.title: Unexpected Result
scenarios.scenario: The high-risk company launches a promising product, but customers do not buy it.

predictionOptions.text: Potential reward does not guarantee an actual return

question.explanation: Even a promising opportunity can perform poorly. Risk exists because the future result is uncertain.

feedback.success: Strong prediction! You recognised that greater reward potential comes with a wider and less certain range of outcomes.

screens.title: A Wider Range of Possibilities
screens.content: You predicted a narrower outcome range for the stable option and a wider range for the high-risk option. Investment risk is the uncertainty that the actual result may differ from what you expect, including the possibility of loss. Investors may accept more risk because an investment offers greater potential returns. However, potential is not a promise. A high-risk investment may earn more, earn less, or lose money. Risk and possible reward are related, but higher risk never guarantees higher profit.
screens.simpleSummary: More potential reward usually means accepting more uncertainty and possible loss.
screens.illustration: Three outcome bands widen from Stable to Moderate to High Risk, extending towards both gains and losses.

screens.title: Freelance Income or New Business?
screens.content: Sara can keep her freelance income in a stable reserve or use some to launch an untested online business. The business could grow quickly, but it might earn nothing. Its higher potential reward comes from taking greater uncertainty—not from a guaranteed profit.
screens.illustration: Sara’s money splits between a stable reserve and a new online-business path with wide possible outcomes.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on the relationship between potential return, uncertainty, and possible loss.
The mission describes risk as uncertainty and presents higher potential returns alongside wider possible gains and losses.
The mission uses adult savings, freelancing, business decisions, portfolios, and straightforward investment comparisons.
All options, amounts, conditions, and outcomes are fictional classroom examples.
The mission repeatedly states that higher risk and greater potential reward do not guarantee profit.
No real investment, company, stock, or future price is discussed.
Stable, moderate, and high-risk choices are compared through trade-offs without presenting one as universally correct.
The mission explains that lower-risk options still carry inflation and other risks, while high-risk options can produce gains or losses.
The mission uses pounds, savings, freelancing, business launches, investment options, and familiar adult financial choices.
The learner predicts narrow, moderate, and wide outcome ranges and compares favourable and difficult conditions.
The quiz directly addresses guaranteed profit, uncertainty, wider outcome ranges, and risks in relatively stable options.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission uses three short story screens, six prediction questions, and three concise quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is practical, clear, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
